hypothesis: At fine sampling (N=256), per-step acceleration is 16x smaller relative to orbit size than at N=64. Next-step prediction can then be done almost entirely by finite-difference (curvature) extrapolation of recent inputs, a heuristic that needs no gravity representation, so accel_step and force margins over control shrink below the N=64 values (accel_step 0.18-0.21, force 0.17-0.21; runs run-20261011-202614-091d and run-20261011-202614-8650).
expected_if_true: In both seeds at the final checkpoint: accel_step margin <= 0.12 and force margin <= 0.12 (at or near the 0.1 threshold), while distance still beats control by >= 0.3 and val_mse_ratio < 1. Taken with the N=16 run, margins fall as N grows.
expected_if_false: In both seeds, accel_step margin >= 0.15 and force margin >= 0.15, which is comparable to N=64. That would mean the gravity structure appears whatever its share of the prediction target, and argues against a pure task-demand account.
